claim: For a single worker paid $32 an hour (the typical production/nonsupervisory wage, $32.38 in June 2026, rounded) adding 400 hours a year, both paths pay $19,200 gross at $48 an hour. Only the half-time premium, $6,400 (33% of the overtime pay), is deductible, and only from federal income tax; payroll tax of $1,468.80 applies either way. Federal income tax on the extra pay is $2,816 as overtime versus $4,224 at a second job, so overtime keeps $14,915 versus $13,507: $1,408 more a year (total federal tax on the extra pay 22.3% vs 29.6%). A second job would have to pay about $53.00 an hour to leave the same take-home as overtime at $48.

100 x ot_premium_deduction_usd / extra_pay_usd. Rounded to 2 decimals.

Income tax on extra, overtime path. Federal income tax T(x) on taxable income x with the 2026 single schedule: 10% up to 12,400; 12% 12,400-50,400; 22% 50,400-105,700; 24% 105,700-201,775; 32% 201,775-256,225; 35% 256,225-640,600; 37% above. Base wages B = regular_rate_usd x 2080. Extra pay E = ot_rate_usd x 400 (8 h x 50 weeks). Income tax on extra = T(B + E - 16100 - D) - T(B - 16100), where D = min(premium, 12500) for overtime and D = 0 for the side job. Payroll tax = 0.0765 x E. Take-home on extra = E - 0.0765 x E - income tax on extra. Rounded to cents.

Income tax on extra, side-job path (D = 0). Federal income tax T(x) on taxable income x with the 2026 single schedule: 10% up to 12,400; 12% 12,400-50,400; 22% 50,400-105,700; 24% 105,700-201,775; 32% 201,775-256,225; 35% 256,225-640,600; 37% above. Base wages B = regular_rate_usd x 2080. Extra pay E = ot_rate_usd x 400 (8 h x 50 weeks). Income tax on extra = T(B + E - 16100 - D) - T(B - 16100), where D = min(premium, 12500) for overtime and D = 0 for the side job. Payroll tax = 0.0765 x E. Take-home on extra = E - 0.0765 x E - income tax on extra. Rounded to cents.
0.0765 x extra_pay_usd (6.2% social security + 1.45% medicare, employee share; same on both paths).
100 x (1 - ot_extra_take_home_usd / extra_pay_usd): federal income + payroll tax as a share of the extra overtime pay. Rounded to 2 decimals.
100 x (1 - side_extra_take_home_usd / extra_pay_usd). Rounded to 2 decimals.
Side-job hourly rate R at which take-home on 400 side-job hours (E = R x 400, D = 0, formula above) equals ot_extra_take_home_usd; solved by bisection on [ot_rate, 3 x ot_rate]. Rounded to cents.

assumptions: Tax year 2026, single filer, standard deduction ($16,100), no other income, no dependents or credits.
Regular job: 40 hours x 52 weeks at the regular rate; extra work: 8 hours a week for 50 weeks (400 hours).

Overtime is required by federal overtime law (over 40 hours in a workweek) at exactly 1.5 times the regular rate and reported by the employer as qualified overtime compensation; only the 0.5x premium is deductible.
The second job is W-2 employment paying the same hourly amount as the overtime rate (no self-employment tax); its hours are not overtime.
Modified AGI stays below $150,000, so the full deduction applies; social security wage base not reached.
Federal taxes only (income tax plus employee payroll tax); state and local taxes ignored.
